title: How Are Animals Sorted? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A sponge, a jellyfish and a cockroach sit on one page of Diya's zoology book. One has no organs, one has no head, one has six jointed legs, yet all three are animals. With over a million animal species described, how do biologists sort them all?

You will see why animals are sorted by body plan and not by looks, then labelled living diagrams of a sponge (ostia, spongocoel, osculum), a jellyfish and a cockroach. We build the six bases of classification from NCERT: level of organisation, symmetry, germ layers, coelom, segmentation and notochord, run all three animals through them, compare a jellyfish with a starfish, and draw the branching map of Kingdom Animalia. Then a worked example with an earthworm, the exam trap about sponges, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 31 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
